description.text: We conduct substantially all of our business activities discussed in this Annual Report on Form 10-K through MSG Sports, LLC and its direct and indirect subsidiaries. The Company was originally incorporated in Delaware on March 4, 2015 as an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of MSG Networks Inc. (“MSG Networks”). All of the outstanding common stock of the Company was distributed to MSG Networks stockholders (the “MSGS Distribution”) on September 30, 2015. On April 17, 2020, the Company distributed all of the outstanding common stock of Sphere Entertainment Co. (formerly Madison Square Garden Entertainment Corp. and referred to herein as “Sphere Entertainment”) to its stockholders (the “Sphere Distribution”). On July 9, 2021, MSG Networks merged with a subsidiary of Sphere Entertainment and became a wholly-owned subsidiary of Sphere Entertainment. Accordingly, agreements between the Company and MSG Networks are now effectively agreements with Sphere Entertainment on a consolidated basis. On April 20, 2023 (the “MSGE Distribution Date”), Sphere Entertainment distributed approximately 67% of the issued and outstanding shares of common stock of Madison Square Garden Entertainment Corp. (referred to herein as “MSG Entertainment”) to its stockholders (the “MSGE Distribution”).

analysis_md:
# MSGS — Madison Square Garden Sports Corp.

Engine 5.5 run, 2026-10-20. Price $400.00 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap $9.701B — in scope under $40B.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Owner of the New York Knicks (NBA) and New York Rangers (NHL), plus the Westchester Knicks and Hartford Wolf Pack development teams and the MSG Training Center. It does not own Madison Square Garden arena (that is MSG Entertainment) — it pays to play there, with lease liabilities of $901,809,000 in dcf_numbers.json against net debt of only $94.0M. Revenue is tickets, suites, sponsorship/signage, local and national media rights, and food/beverage/merchandise. A separation is imminent in the research: the Rangers business is expected to be spun off (record date October 20, 2026, distribution scheduled October 26, 2026 in the search results), leaving a Knicks company — the combined OE history below will not describe either post-spin company.

## Owner's earnings
FY2026 (10-K, period ended 2026-06-30, from financials_history.csv): revenue $1,153,822,000, operating cash flow $62,663,000, capex $1,407,000, SBC $21,524,000.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2026: $39,732,000 = $1.64/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE total $39.7M, latest FY OE/share $1.64)
- Maintenance version FY2026 (financials_history.csv): $36,142,000 — same ballpark as the conservative figure.
- **Base used = median of last 3 FY OE/share: $2.88/share** (key_numbers.md; FY2024 $2.88, FY2025 $2.91, FY2026 $1.64 in financials_history.csv). No TTM pin: the FY ended only 3.7 months ago (key_numbers.md diagnostics), so there is no STALE_FY flag and the median is the engine base.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years (key_numbers.md), but thin: operating income was only $28,868,000 on $1,153,822,000 of revenue in FY2026 (financials_history.csv). Net debt $94.0M is 1.35x normalized OE (key_numbers.md) before the $901,809,000 of lease liabilities noted above.
- This is the central method limit: the franchises are carried at historical cost and book equity is negative (-$263,296,000 in the latest financials_history.csv row), so the cash-flow OE stream is a small fraction of the asset value the market is pricing. The DCF below is a cash-flow verdict, not a sum-of-the-parts verdict.

## Moat: 7/10 — strong scarcity, weak cash capture
Justification: territorial exclusivity for the only NBA and NHL franchises in New York, irreplaceable scarcity, and proven per-game pricing power, held back because players/leagues capture much of the surplus and local media rights fell in FY2026.
- FOR: Territorial exclusivity — the only NBA (Knicks) and NHL (Rangers) franchises in the New York market; irreplaceable scarcity (no new franchise can be created in this market); proven pricing power — per-game ticket, suite and sponsorship revenues rose in FY2026 even with fewer home games in Q3; national media rights step-up from the new NBA deals that began in 2025-26; the Knicks' 2026 championship run showed operating leverage (about $182M postseason revenue in FY2026 per research summaries of the filing).
- AGAINST: Players capture the surplus — rising team compensation and luxury tax, plus a new NHL revenue-sharing formula, pressure FY2027; local media rights fees fell in FY2026 after the MSG Networks restructuring; revenue is performance-volatile and the Rangers missed the playoffs two straight years; Dolan family voting control and related-party arena arrangements; a Section 162(m) tax change flagged in research as about $60M of added annual tax from FY2028.
- ROIC / margin evidence (required check): fundamentals.json reports no gross-margin series (no COGS filing) and its roic_proxy series is unusable — it swings from -1.61 to +4.79 in recent years in fundamentals.json because book equity is negative. That is a written reason the measured history understates the franchise: the assets are carried at historical cost, not at the private franchise values research cites (Sportico estimates in the search results put the Knicks and Rangers together well above the $9.701B market cap). A 7 sits on scarcity and pricing power, not on measured ROIC, and pass 2 should attack exactly that gap.
- A 7 gives CAP = 11.1 years (key_numbers.md): growth holds 2 years, then converges to 2.5% terminal over 11.1 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-20)
Growth recalibration (written reason): the engine blend is 10.00% (key_numbers.md), but its components are unreliable here — rev CAGR 5y 22.65% is a COVID-rebound / post-spin artefact, OE/share CAGR 2y is -24.59%, rev CAGR 3y is 9.14% and latest rev YoY is 11.03%, with the FY2026 print boosted by a championship playoff run that will not repeat on schedule. Scenario starts were therefore recalibrated downward via offsets -0.12 / -0.07 / -0.05 / -0.02 / +0.02 to -2.0% / 3.0% / **5.0%** / 8.0% / 12.0%: the base start sits below the latest print because that print contains the playoff boost and the national-media step-up, and even the super-bull start (12.0%) is only just above the latest 11.03% YoY. Probabilities 15/30/30/15/10 put 45% on bear-or-worse for OE volatility (see flags); OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | -2.0% | 0.75 | $14.34 | 2.91% |
| Bear | 30% | 3.0% | 0.90 | $21.76 | 3.19% |
| Base | 30% | 5.0% | 1.00 | $26.58 | 3.37% |
| Bull | 15% | 8.0% | 1.10 | $33.70 | 3.66% |
| Super bull | 10% | 12.0% | 1.25 | $46.31 | 4.18% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $26.34 (-93.4% vs price), IV@12% $35.07, IV@10% $44.83, weighted IRR 3.37%, base-case IRR 3.37%** (key_numbers.md)
- **Tier by numbers: D; bear tier D, bull tier D** (key_numbers.md IRR band 3.19% to 3.66%). Diagnostics: OE yield 0.72%, terminal value 19.0% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.23x, net debt 1.35x normalized OE, 3.7 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT**: named — the April 2020 spin-off of MSG Entertainment and the COVID collapse/recovery straddle the 5-year window. In financials_history.csv, PP&E falls from $1,253,671,000 (FY2018 row as filed in that history) to the post-spin scale and capex falls from $363,475,000 in FY2020 to $466,000 in FY2021, D&A from $93,362,000 to $5,574,000, and revenue fell to $415,721,000 in FY2021 before recovering. No scenario start was taken from the 22.65% 5-year CAGR; starts were set from the 3-year CAGR, the latest print and the playoff adjustment above.
- **OE_VOLATILE**: real — OE/share in financials_history.csv spans $6.26 (FY2022) and $5.21 (FY2023) down to $1.64 (FY2026), and was negative in FY2020-21. Handled with the 3-year median base and 45% weight on bear-or-worse; confidence is low.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE (2025, 2026)**: net income was -$22,438,000 in FY2025 and $7,759,000 in FY2026 against OCF of $91,607,000 and $62,663,000 (financials_history.csv), while D&A was only $3,218,000 and $3,179,000 — the gap is not D&A. The CSV's delta_nwc is -$62,869,000 in FY2025 and -$26,611,000 in FY2026 (a working-capital inflow, i.e. advance ticket/suite/sponsorship receipts in deferred revenue ahead of the season), which is the main bridge; the OCF-based conservative OE is the series used throughout, and its FY2026 figure is corroborated by the maintenance OE of $36,142,000 in the same CSV.
- **IRR_AT_FLOOR (super bear)**: accepted as stated — at $400.00 the price is beyond the model's range and the super-bear return reads 'at most ~3.0%', not the recorded 2.91%. The weighted IRR is not at the floor (score.json irr_at_floor: false).
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE (latest $1.64 vs median $2.88)**: the latest year is the lower, more current figure — OCF fell from $91,607,000 (FY2025) to $62,663,000 (FY2026) despite revenue rising 11.03%, while SBC rose from $17,935,000 to $21,524,000 (financials_history.csv). The median is not obviously distorted (FY2024-25 both printed about $2.9), so the median was kept as the base and the divergence is a reason for low confidence, not for a pin: even on the median the weighted IV@15% is $26.34, so the choice does not change the tier.
- **LOW_OE_YIELD (0.72%)**: accepted — the valuation the market pays rests on franchise asset appreciation and the pending spin-off, not on current OE growth. That is exactly why confidence is low and the verdict is sized to the cash-flow end.

## My thoughts / method range
- The honest headline is the method gap: on owner's earnings this is a clear D, with every scenario — including super bull at 4.18% IRR — far below the 15% hurdle, and the hurdle-clearing price is $26.34 (key_numbers.md). On a sum-of-the-parts / private-franchise-value basis, research cited in the searches values the two franchises above the current market cap. Both statements can be true; this sweep scores only the first.
- The pending Rangers spin-off (record date today in the research) will break this combined history: the next run for either successor should be treated as a new basis, not a refresh of this score.
- Risks not in the OE path: player-cost and luxury-tax escalation, the local-media reset, the FY2028 tax change noted in the moat section, Dolan-control discount, and a non-repeat championship year hitting FY2027 comparisons.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 3.37%; no tier override)
- Confidence: **Low** (OE-volatile, franchise value outside the cash-flow model, spin-off pending)
- One-liner: Irreplaceable franchises, moat 7/10, but owner's earnings do not capture franchise appreciation — Tier D on cash flow (3.37% weighted IRR, IV@15% $26.34 vs $400 price); clears 15% only below $26.34, so the price is an asset-value / spin-off bet, not an OE bet.
